observations: Register provider or Save provider with an issuer that cannot be reached shows only 'The change could not be saved. Try again.' The guide's advice (correct the issuer URL or its reachability) is right, but the app does not say discovery failed.
An SMTP server with an smtp:// prefix or a port is refused with the generic 'One or more request fields are invalid.' The guide's instruction (host name only, no prefix, no port) prevents it.

The author's open limitation on a sign-in link whose method was turned off is settled: the link opens /portal/login with 'This sign-in link could not be used. Request a new link or contact your administrator.' and no session.

On the shared work2 lab, the first org run hit 'Too many sign-in link requests. Try again later.' for the seeded Business User Jonas Weber (3 link requests per address per 15 minutes, 30 per client address), because other walkthrough agents also request links for him. The guide does not describe this limit. The recorded run used a fresh Portal-created Business User.
limitations: SAML: the app has no SAML setup. The Identity provider card offers OpenID Connect fields only (Provider ID, Issuer URL, Email domain, Client ID, Client secret). The scenario's SAML fixture check cannot run; the guide says 'it has no SAML setup interface'.

The OIDC identity provider is a local fixture (oauth2-mock-server 9.2.0, the API test dependency) in container openlaw-docs-80ceef9e-auth2-oidc-1 on the lab network as http://oidc:8080. The browser reached it through a Chromium host-resolver mapping. The existing openlaw-keycloak container was not used.

operator is a responsibility, not an account. Operator steps were deployment changes on the owned labs (phase.sh recreates app and worker with compose overlays overlay-mail-*.json and overlay-baseurl-unset.json), followed by browser checks as the lab Administrator.

With BASE_URL removed, the API accepts requests only from its default origin http://localhost:3000. The Administrator reached the lab at that address through a browser host mapping to the lab port, as an operator would on the host itself.

There is no control to remove a saved logo. The walkthrough restored the shared lab's original logo (none) through PATCH /api/v1/org/general after the check. The organization name and logo on work2 were changed for about a minute.

The promoted-Business-User Invited branch needs an account that never signed in; a Portal-created Business User always has, so the row stayed Active as the guide expects. The branch itself was not reproduced.
Upgrade-time email logo copies ('Logos saved before email logos existed') were not exercised: the labs were built fresh at 067c1646.
The unseeded wizard lab auth2w was a second owned lab, because the seeded auth2 lab has finished first-run setup.
scriptNotes: After the auth2w and auth2 policy, sso and twoFactor runs, two helpers changed: requestMagicLink no longer clicks 'Email me a sign-in link' when the page opens straight on the link form, and passwordSignIn records 'password-not-offered' when a page has no password choice. Both paths only change behavior when the choice is missing; in those runs every choice was present. The org and crossPage runs used the final script.
crossPage starts by resetting both policies to the lab default through the policy API, because an earlier failed development run left Business Email and password off.
Development runs are kept under runs/superseded/ and are not credited.
